run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:38:18Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a low but persistent stream of HTTP 503 responses that frontend-proxy (Envoy) returned to the load generator because its upstream, the frontend service, terminated connections before sending response headers ("upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}"). The error rate is small (measured 5-minute span-error ratio 0.0004-0.0033; 0.0016 in the 10 minutes to 23:38:30, ~30s after the alert started) and the affected requests carry no frontend server span, so the failure point is the frontend's socket handling, not a downstream response. The only fault-injection flag switched on in otel-demo/flagd-config is productCatalogFailure = "on" ("Fail product catalog service on a specific product"), and the only workload that changed in the window is the product-catalog Deployment, rolled out to a new ReplicaSet at 23:30:53 with a new pod at restartCount 0; that rollout is the strongest single candidate for the cause, and the largest 5-minute error bucket (23:28-23:33) coincides with it and with the frontend's own tcp.connect error. However, the declared productCatalogFailure effect was not observed (product-catalog spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, GetProduct p95 stayed ~1.9 ms), the 503s also occur well before and after the rollout, and neither the flag change time nor the trigger of the rollout can be seen, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error-status spans are exactly the span operation "ingress" with http.status_code 503; error spans were present from the earliest available sample (2026-11-17T23:08:18Z) through 23:48:18Z at roughly 1.1-10 spans per 5 minutes, and the 5-minute error ratio of frontend-proxy ingress spans reached 0.0029-0.0033 in the 23:33-23:37 interval and was 0.0016 at 23:38:30, 30 seconds after the alert started.

frontend-proxy's own access log records the failures as "GET /api/products/...", "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=..." and "GET /api/cart" returning "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" at 23:28:45, 23:30:53, 23:31:47, 23:36:50, 23:37:21, 23:42:09, 23:45:37 and 23:46:23 - i.e. the upstream (cluster "frontend") closed the connection before response headers, while the same log shows normal 200 "via_upstream" traffic in between.

The sampled 503 traces (2026-11-17T23:08:12Z-23:25:57Z) contain only load-generator "GET" (503) -> frontend-proxy "ingress" (503) -> frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" (error="true", http.status_code=0); the whole trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 has exactly these four spans and no span from the frontend service, so the aborted requests never produced a frontend server span.

The frontend's own ERROR-status spans are confined to the 5-minute interval 23:28-23:33: frontend "GET" 5.56, "POST" 1.11, "POST /api/checkout" 1.11, "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout" 1.11 and "tcp.connect" 1.11 error spans; in the following buckets (23:33-23:48) frontend's product-page, cart, checkout and gRPC spans all read 0 error spans.

The otel-demo Deployment product-catalog was rolled out at 23:30:53: "Scaled up replica set product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1", the new pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 was Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 23:30:53-23:30:56, and "Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0" deleted pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp at 23:30:57; the new pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and the new ReplicaSet was created 23:30:53 while the old ReplicaSet has 0 replicas.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has the fault-injection flag "productCatalogFailure" set to defaultVariant "on" with description "Fail product catalog service on a specific product" (state ENABLED), while every other flag in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) is "off"; productCatalogFailure is therefore a switched-on setting whose name refers to the product-catalog service that was redeployed in the window.

No object other than the product-catalog Deployment is seen applying a change or fault to product-catalog: the only otel-demo events inside the authorized window are the nine product-catalog rollout events (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet x2), and all other events in the window belong to namespace data-recorders.

product-catalog's own telemetry shows no failure: its spans in the 45 minutes to 23:57 carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 23630, ListProducts 2059) and GetProduct p95 latency stayed flat between 1.913 and 1.924 ms across 23:15-23:50.

Cluster and pod state is clean: all 21 otel-demo pods (including frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 and product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9) are Phase Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, all five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure False, the frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog Services have populated endpoints (frontend 100.96.3.42), and there are no NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas in the cluster.

frontend runs under a 100m CPU / 200Mi memory limit (frontend-proxy 30m/50Mi, product-catalog 15m/30Mi); the frontend container was CPU-throttled on 24-31% of CFS periods throughout 23:15-23:50, used only 120-131 MB of memory (container_memory_usage_bytes, working set 240-262 MB including file cache), and showed frontend "GET" p95 latency of 152-227 ms and frontend-proxy ingress p95 of 368-660 ms with no sustained degradation across the sampled window.

A second configuration-style replacement happened earlier in the window: ReplicaSet flagd-8d6d7b54 was created at 22:59:40 and pod flagd-8d6d7b54-hjfkl started at 22:59:40 with 0 restarts, while the original ReplicaSet flagd-c47676d99 (created 22:57:52) now has 0 replicas; flagd-config's resourceVersion (1600742) is higher than product-catalog-products' (1591781), i.e. the flag ConfigMap is the more recently written of the two.

The switched-on productCatalogFailure flag in flagd-config is the likely origin of the 503s: product-catalog returns an error for one specific product, and frontend API routes that render that product abort the HTTP connection before writing headers - which is consistent with Envoy logging "upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" and with the aborted requests producing no frontend server span - while the product-catalog Deployment rollout at 23:30:53 is consistent with the configuration being re-applied.

The largest error bucket (23:28-23:33, 10 frontend-proxy ingress error spans of which 6.67 egress error spans, plus the frontend's only error spans and one tcp.connect failure) is a transient caused by the product-catalog pod replacement at 23:30:53-23:30:57, when the frontend could not connect to the terminating/new product-catalog pod; this would explain that burst but not the 503s seen before 23:30 or at 23:42-23:46.

An alternative that remains open is an intrinsic intermittent upstream-connection termination between Envoy and the frontend (for example an idle keep-alive connection closed exactly as a request is sent), which would produce isolated "UC" 503s without any frontend-side span or error signal; most 5-minute buckets show frontend-proxy ingress errors with no matching frontend error spans, which fits this explanation as well as the flag explanation.

The effect declared by the switched-on flag was not observed: no product-catalog span carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR, GetProduct p95 is flat (~1.9 ms), and the frontend's ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, product-page and cart API-route error counts are 0 in every 5-minute bucket from 23:33 to 23:48, so the productCatalogFailure fault itself was not caught happening.

The frontend and frontend-proxy pods are healthy in their own signals: restartCount 0 with no previous terminated state, memory usage 120-131 MB against the 200Mi limit, and frontend-proxy logs show continuous successful 200 "via_upstream" responses (for example at 23:27:05-23:27:14) between the 503 events.

The 503s are not confined to the product-catalog rollout: error spans appear from the first available sample at 23:08:18 onward (e.g. 2.64 error spans in the 2 minutes to 23:10:18) and continue at 23:42:09, 23:45:37 and 23:46:23, well after the rollout completed at 23:30:57, so the rollout alone does not explain the whole error rate.

A frontend OOM kill or crash-restart is not the mechanism: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw has restartCount 0, an empty lastState and a start time of 22:57:51Z, and its memory usage (120-131 MB) stays below the 200Mi limit, so it was not restarted during the incident.

A Service/endpoint or network-policy misconfiguration blocking frontend-proxy -> frontend is not supported: the frontend Service has endpoint 100.96.3.42, no NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas exist, and the large majority of requests return 200, so connectivity is not generally blocked.

Verify the intended value of productCatalogFailure in otel-demo/flagd-config and obtain the feature-flag change history, since it is the only fault flag switched on and its state cannot be time-stamped from the current object.

Inspect the frontend (Next.js) server behaviour for aborted requests around 23:28-23:38 and consider whether a RequestErrorRate rule with an "above 0" threshold is appropriate for this environment, because the observed error ratio is only 0.04%-0.33% of ingress spans.

gaps: The alert's own rule is not available: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name "RequestErrorRate" returned no data, so the exact expression and window behind the annotation's "current: 0.01111111111111111" are unknown and that value could not be reproduced from traces_span_metrics_calls_total, which read a 5-minute error ratio of 0.0016 at 23:38:30.

Feature-flag/change history is not integrated, so it is unknown when productCatalogFailure was switched to "on", who changed it, and what triggered the product-catalog Deployment rollout at 23:30:53 (Deployment generation 2, revision 2).

kube_pod_container_info returned no series for otel-demo/product-catalog-* in the window, so the image digests of the replaced and the new product-catalog pod could not be compared and the rollout could not be confirmed as configuration-only. Jaeger retained no frontend-proxy or frontend traces after about 23:26 (searches for 23:31-23:38 returned nothing), so the traces behind the 23:28-23:33 burst and the alert instant 23:38:18 are unknown.

Application logs are largely unavailable: the frontend container returned no log lines for 23:00-23:58, and error-pattern queries on product-catalog and flagd containers matched no lines; the frontend-proxy log read was also incomplete (4 MiB read limit reached, newest 100 of 13668 matching lines for 23:00-23:27 and 9 of 13423 lines read through 23:47 for the 503 filter), so no application-level error text confirms what the frontend or product-catalog did at all failure times.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket returned no series for frontend-proxy and product-catalog, so gRPC status codes of product-catalog GetProduct calls could not be checked; a gRPC error recorded with Unset span status would be invisible in the available span metrics.

The flagd Deployment was also replaced during the window (ReplicaSet flagd-8d6d7b54 created 22:59:40, old flagd-c47676d99 at 0 replicas); this change could not be attributed to this cause or to another one and is recorded as an unresolved change.
The measured trace data starts only at 23:08:18, so the pre-incident baseline for frontend-proxy error rate and latency is unknown and no latency trend can be inferred.
next_steps: Check the flagd flag change log or GitOps history for demo.flagd.json to see when productCatalogFailure became "on" and confirm whether that value is intended.
Capture the frontend container's stderr/stdout and Next.js server errors during a reproduction of the 503 UC events, and confirm whether API-route exceptions abort the socket.
Review the RequestErrorRate alert expression and its window against the observed 0.04%-0.33% error ratio to decide whether the "above 0" threshold is meaningful here.
Confirm whether the product-catalog Deployment change at 23:30:53 was a configuration-only rollout (image digest comparison from the old pod) and what object triggered it.
